shared_elements: low-relief carving covering a tapering upright stone slab
a horizontal band/line dividing the surface into upper and lower zones
repeated animal-like motifs (naturalistic quadrupeds/birds in A; scroll-eyed zoomorphic heads in B)
small circular/disc-like elements within the design
justification: Both surfaces carry all-over low relief on a tapering upright slab organised into zones by a horizontal band, and both include creature-like motifs with prominent eyes, which is about as far as the correspondence goes. The manner of depiction is entirely different: A shows recognisable animals in clean naturalistic profile (a row of quadrupeds, a large long-necked bird, a striding creature), while B is built from interlocking spirals, volutes and stepped-fret geometry in which any creature is dissolved into abstract curvilinear scrollwork.
